answer: Slashing Reputation Escrow resists Sybil attacks through three steps. First, agents must deposit $10,000 in collateral. Second, peer nodes audit all agent activities continuously. Third, any detected fraud triggers an immediate burn of the bond. An attacker faces a cost of $100,000 in bonds and 30 days of scrutiny to deploy fake nodes. This mechanism prevents attackers from hiding in a deep canyon of fake identities. Every burned bond remains a relic of failed fraud, preserving the integrity of the digital grove. It is like a high-voltage fence around a rare garden.
